newsitem.title: USA: Most US spot resids slip again on stocks, weather.
newsitem.headline: Most US spot resids slip again on stocks, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly lost grouund again Monday despite the recent cold snap, still undermined by oversupply and forecasts for milder East Coast weather by midweek, industry sources said.

"By the time we get to the Super Bowl, buyers start looking for pieces, not cargoes. Barring any unforseen cold, winter may be over," said one trader, referring to the January 26 U.S. football championship playoff game.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to $17.50-75 amid little interest. February one percent paper sold at $17, off more than a quarter from Friday's levels.
NYH 2.2 percent was talked on either side of $17, also modestly lower, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped 35 cents to $16.25-50 though some thought the number was lower after a reported, but unconfirmed, January deal for 50,000 barrels (eight gravity) at $16.
USG three percent again was off slightly to about $15.25.

The prospect for milder New York weather this week tanked city gate gas prices by $2 to about $4.00/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid eased to a $2.80/mmBtu equivalent. February city gate gas was quoted at 75 cents over the screen, or at about $3.85/mmBtu, versus February resid paper at a $2.70/mmBtu equivalent.
